source: ASME B16.10-2022 (Revision of ASME B16.10-2017), incorporating the March 2023 errata to Tables 1.3-1 and 1.3-3. Transcribed from a purchased copy held outside version control.
note: The length of a valve. B16.34 says how much pressure a valve holds and at what temperature; it says nothing about how long it is. Without B16.10 a spool cannot be dimensioned, an isometric cannot be closed and an MTO pipe length is a guess.

dimensionSymbols.D: centre-to-face, angle valves with flanged ends
dimensionSymbols.E: centre-to-end, angle valves with buttwelding ends

conventions.aAndBAreOneFigure: A column headed "A and B" prints ONE number that serves both the flanged face-to-face and the buttwelding end-to-end. Two rows are emitted from it so that a query by end type does not have to know that, but they carry the same figure and the same source column.
conventions.oneColumnManyValveTypes: B16.10 groups valve types that share a length - "Globe, Lift Check, and Swing Check" is one column. valveTypes is therefore a list, and a globe valve and a swing check of the same class and size are the same length by the standard, not by coincidence.
conventions.steelOnly: Class 125 and 250 CAST IRON columns, and the AWWA patterns, are read and skipped. ASME B16.34 - which supplies the rating - does not cover cast iron, and the material library holds no cast-iron valve body. 478 cast-iron cells were parsed and discarded.
conventions.facingChangesTheLength: These figures are for the facing named in the table (1.5 mm raised face for Classes 150 and 300, 6.4 mm for 600 and above). A ring joint or a tongue-and-groove face changes the length. See facingAdjustments and ringJoint - a dimension quoted without the facing is incomplete.
conventions.erratum: The March 2023 erratum corrected misaligned column headings on pages 13 and 21 (Tables 1.3-1 and 1.3-3). The corrected pages are bound at the FRONT of the PDF, ahead of the title page, so they are parsed last here and overwrite the originals.

anomalies.why: A valve does not get shorter as it gets bigger, and the two unit columns of a table convert into one another - except where B16.10 prints otherwise. Every case below was read off the page before being listed. The known reasons: Table 1.3-1 column 9 takes its large sizes from API 6D (note 14), so the curve is two standards spliced together; Class 900 valves DN 65 and smaller carry CLASS 1500 dimensions by note (2) of Table 1.5-2, which makes the small end of that column longer than the sizes above it. Neither is an error and neither is ours to smooth over.

erratumCheck.note: The corrected pages were parsed and compared cell by cell against the originals bound later in the same file. They agree, so the erratum in this copy changed headings only, not figures - which is exactly what ASME said it did. The column map above was read from the CORRECTED pages.

corroboration.note: B16.10 Table 1.3-1 note (14) says its Class 150 gate figures for the large sizes are "extracted from API 6D". Read from the other side, they are: 17 of 19 sizes match to the millimetre and the other two are the same inch figure rounded differently. Two standards, one set of numbers.
corroboration.explainsADeclaredAnomaly: The B16.10 round declared a monotonicity exception in Table 1.3-1 column 9 - the column shortens from 762 mm at NPS 34 to 711 mm at NPS 36 - and attributed it to note (14). API 6D settles it: 6D gives 813 mm at NPS 36 and 660 mm at NPS 30, and our B16.10 data holds BOTH {711, 813} at NPS 36 and {610, 660} at NPS 30. The larger figure in each pair is the API 6D one; the smaller is the THROUGH-CONDUIT valve that note (14) sends to a different number. The column was never non-monotonic - it was two valve constructions printed in one place.
